slides.title: Ozonolysis makes CH₂OO hot enough to leave the well
slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Motivation · ozonolysis

Ozonolysis makes CH₂OO hot enough to leave the well

C₂H₄ + O₃ forms CH₂OO with up to 48 kcal/mol (about 2.1 eV) above its minimum, the dashed line.

That is above the barriers out of the well, so part of the CH₂OO reacts before collisions can cool it.

Hot molecules sample geometries far from the minimum, where a harmonic or well-only surface does not hold.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 3 · energies: HEAT-345(Q), Nguyen et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 119, 5524 (2015); figure: Simiyu & Smith, ACS Fall 2025
slides.notes: Ozonolysis mechanism: Criegee, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. Engl. 14, 745 (1975). Energies relative to the CH2OO minimum, from the HEAT-345(Q) study of Nguyen, Lee, Matthews, McCarthy and Stanton (J. Phys. Chem. A 2015, 119, 5524-5533), as drawn on our ACS Fall 2025 poster. Ozonolysis releases a broad distribution of energy into CH2OO: some is collisionally stabilized, some decays promptly (to dioxirane over TS 1, and to other products). 48 kcal/mol is about 2.1 eV, comparable to the O-O dissociation region of the NEVPT2 surface later in the deck and above the 0.4-1.8 eV window of the new CCSD(T) shell. That is the regime the surface must handle for ozonolysis-energy IR and branching. Two cautions from Kuwata's 2024 perspective (J. Phys. Chem. A 128, 7331): Nguyen et al. attribute nearly all the OH from ethene ozonolysis to primary-ozonide diradicals rather than to CH2OO, and a significant fraction of small Criegees is formed cold or collisionally stabilized (Kroll et al. 2001). Thermal (stabilised) decomposition of CH2OO and CD2OO, measured directly: Stone, Au, Sime, Medeiros, Blitz, Seakins, Decker and Sheps, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 20, 24940 (2018), cavity-enhanced UV absorption at 450-650 K with MESMER fits: barrier to decomposition (via dioxirane) 81.8 kJ/mol for CH2OO and 80.1 for CD2OO, products 63.7% H2 + CO2, 36.0% H2O + CO and only 0.3% OH + HCO; CD2OO decomposes faster than CH2OO. These are the well-exit channels a surface for hot CH2OO has to reach.

slides.html:
Motivation · prediction

CH₂OO is the test case; larger Criegees are the goal

CH₂OO

Smallest Criegee, with the most data to test against: IR bands, UV spectrum, photodissociation products

Test the method here

CH₃CHOO

syn and anti conformers, told apart by IR, react at very different rates

Lin et al., Nat. Commun. 6, 7012 (2015)

MVK-oxide

Four carbons, from isoprene ozonolysis: conformers, few spectra, kinetics leaning on theory

Vansco et al., PNAS 117, 9733 (2020)

Unimolecular decay to OH depends on how much energy the Criegee carries (Lester & Klippenstein, Acc. Chem. Res. 51, 978, 2018). As molecules grow, experiments thin out: predictions need a surface we trust at high energy, checked first where the data are rich.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 4
slides.notes: The pipeline is meant to carry over: build the surface from a cheap multireference method everywhere plus a coupled-cluster correction where it is valid, check it against spectroscopy, then run dynamics. CH2OO is where every step can be checked. References: Lin, Huang, Wang et al., Nature Communications 6, 7012 (2015), syn- and anti-CH3CHOO by step-scan IR; Vansco et al., PNAS 117, 9733-9740 (2020), isoprene-derived methyl vinyl ketone oxide; Lester and Klippenstein, Acc. Chem. Res. 51, 978 (2018), prompt and thermal decay of Criegee intermediates to OH.

slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Motivation · state of the art

What a Criegee model must get right (Kuwata, 2024)

Kuwata’s perspectivewhat it means for this project
Conformation decides the fate: syn-alkyl CIs shift H to vinyl hydroperoxides and OH; CH₂OO and anti CIs close to dioxirane or react with waterthe method has to carry over to conformers of CH₃CHOO and MVK-oxide
Ground-state reactivity: single-reference CCSD(T) with transition state theory agrees with experimentsupports CCSD(T) for the well and the shell
UV spectra need multireference methods with large active spaces and at least second-order dynamic correlation; EOM-CCSD is 0.2 eV too highour NEVPT2 network uses (8,6): test it against (12,10) before the UV benchmark
CH₂OO UV structure comes from the B/C avoided crossing near r(O–O) 2.1 Å, modelled in r(O–O), ∠COO and r(C–O)the same coordinates as our surface; needs the B and C states and their coupling: the diabatic network
Roaming in vinyl hydroperoxide decay needs static and dynamic correlation and variational rate theorydynamics on an ML surface can treat it directly, as trajectories on a global ab initio surface did for complex-forming H + HCCH collisions seen by IR emission (Smith et al., JACS 136, 1682, 2014)

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 6 · K. T. Kuwata, J. Phys. Chem. A 128, 7331–7345 (2024), doi 10.1021/acs.jpca.4c04517
slides.notes: Kuwata, "Computational Modeling of the Conformation-Dependent Atmospheric Reactivity of Criegee Intermediates," J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 7331-7345 (Perspective). Points used here: (1) syn-alkyl and syn-vinyl CIs isomerize quickly to vinyl hydroperoxides or dioxoles; CH2OO and anti CIs prefer dioxirane closure or bimolecular reaction (water, SO2). (2) Single-reference methods with conventional TST and Eckart tunneling have matched experiment for ground-state reactivity. (3) For the CH2OO B-X spectrum, MRCI+Q-F12b(18,14) gives vertical excitation 3.75-3.83 eV, EOM-CCSD 4.01 eV (too high: no static correlation); CASPT2(12,10) beat (10,8) and MRCI(10,8) (McCoy et al.), so a larger active space matters more than the level of dynamic correlation; TDDFT is about 0.7 eV too blue. For MVK-oxide smaller active spaces, including (8,6), shifted lambda-max 50-100 nm red. (4) Nikoobakht and Koppel trace the vibrational structure to the B/C avoided crossing near R(O-O) 2.1 A, using R(O-O), theta(COO) and R(C-O): the coordinates of our 3-D surface. (5) Roaming of OH in vinyl hydroperoxide decay needs multireference electronic structure and variational TST. Our related precedent: Smith, Nikow, Ma, Wilhelm, Han, Sharma, Bowman and Dai, 'Chemical Activation through Super Energy Transfer Collisions,' J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 1682-1685: hot H atoms (about 60 kcal/mol) form a transient complex with HCCH, and about 10% of collisions leave up to 70% of the energy in acetylene vibration, seen by time-resolved IR emission and reproduced by quasi-classical trajectories on a global ab initio potential (Bowman group). Long-lived complexes on a flat region of the surface are the same dynamical regime as roaming, and the same IR-emission and trajectory tools apply. Also noted: Nguyen et al. attribute almost all OH from ethene ozonolysis to primary-ozonide diradicals, not to CH2OO.

slides.title: Spectra from dynamics on a learned surface
slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Approach · ACS Fall 2025

Spectra from dynamics on a learned surface

Surface = energy + Δ + dipole. Dynamics on it, then the Fourier transform of the dipole autocorrelation gives a spectrum to compare with experiment.

Since the poster, for CH₂OO:

a full 9-D CCSD(T) surface for the well, quantum vibrations (VCI) and ring-polymer dynamics to test it, and a quasi-diabatic NEVPT2 network with Δ-learning for the excited states and hot molecules.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 7 · B. N. Simiyu and J. M. Smith, poster, ACS Fall 2025 National Meeting
slides.notes: Figure 1 of the poster: Simiyu and Smith, "Vibrational spectral prediction of transient species using machine learning potential energy surfaces," ACS Fall 2025 (Temple University; Hylleraas Centre, University of Oslo). There the surfaces were trained on importance-sampled points from DFT (B3LYP/cc-pVTZ) direct dynamics, with CCSD(T) and a Delta correction; the example panels show a small test molecule (O-H stretch and torsion). The rest of this deck is the sequence of refinements that took CH2OO from that protocol to agreement with experiment, and why each was needed.

Three independent checks on the same surface: exact quantum vibrations (VCI) with rotational contours, ring-polymer dynamics converged in bead number, and the isotopologues CD₂OO, ¹³CH₂OO, CH₂¹⁸O¹⁸O and CHDOO. slides.notes: The one-slide answer. Surface: CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVDZ at 3,613 geometries in all nine internal coordinates, plus a 9-D aug-cc-pVTZ minus aug-cc-pVDZ correction from 250 points, fitted as an order-5 Cs-symmetric polynomial (held-out error 0.59 meV within 0.8 eV of the minimum). Fundamentals (VCI, cm-1) against Huang et al. 2015 (0.25 cm-1 resolution): nu3 1432.3 / 1434.1, nu4 1275.1 / 1285.9, nu5 1202.5 / 1213.3, nu6 910.0 / 909.26, nu8 853.4 / 847.44; mean absolute error 6.0 cm-1. Published benchmark: Li, Carter, Bowman, Dawes, Xie and Guo, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 5, 2364 (2014), CCSD(T)-F12a/aug-cc-pVTZ, more than 50,000 points, VCI-5 in MULTIMODE: mean absolute error 6.5 cm-1 on the same five bands (values from Chang et al., J. Chem. Phys. 146, 244302 (2017), Table II). The 0.04% is the largest error in the ground-state constants when the vibrational corrections from our surface are added to the semi-experimental equilibrium structure of McCarthy et al.; with the surface's own minimum the constants are about 1% low (bonds slightly long at aug-cc-pVDZ), so the structure, not the vibration-rotation physics, carries the remaining error. Band contour: correlation 0.91 between the computed and measured O-O band, 860-960 cm-1.

slides.title: DVR, the discrete variable representation: quantum levels on a grid
slides.section: Refinements 1-3: a smooth fit, clean data, quantum levels
slides.notes: For an undergraduate audience. The Schrödinger equation for a vibrating bond is a differential equation; on a grid it becomes a matrix equation, which a computer solves in milliseconds. Why it is called discrete variable representation: the unknowns are the values of the wavefunction at discrete points of the variable (here the bond length), and the potential energy matrix is diagonal in that representation, so no integrals over the surface are needed, only its value at each point. The kinetic-energy matrix has a closed form for evenly spaced points (Colbert and Miller, J. Chem. Phys. 96, 1982 (1992)); it is like the finite-difference second derivative of a calculus class, but exact for functions that fit on the grid. Our 3-D and 4-D calculations used the same idea with 28 points per coordinate in 3-D (21,952 grid points) and 20 per coordinate in 4-D. In the figure the stems are the eigenvector entries: v = 0 has no node, v = 1 one node, v = 2 two; the spacing E2 - E1 is about 11% smaller than E1 - E0, which is the anharmonicity. The cost grows as (points per coordinate) to the power of the number of coordinates, which is why the full 9-D problem later uses VCI instead.

slides.title: Why a vibrating, rotating molecule gives two branches
slides.section: Refinement 4: rotation sets the band shape
slides.notes: For an undergraduate audience. The infrared light interacts with the molecule's dipole as seen in the laboratory. A vibrating bond makes the dipole oscillate at nu0; if the molecule also turns, that oscillating dipole points in a direction that rotates at rate omega, and the product cos(2 pi nu0 t) cos(omega t) equals half of cos[(nu0 + omega) t] plus half of cos[(nu0 - omega) t]: two frequencies, exactly like the sidebands of an AM radio signal. That is what each single trajectory on the previous slide shows (splitting equal to twice the rotation rate, r = 0.99). At 300 K the rotation rates follow a Boltzmann distribution (drawn for rotation about two axes, P(omega) proportional to omega exp(-omega^2 / 2 omega_T^2)); summing every molecule's pair of lines gives two smooth lobes, the P branch (lower wavenumber) and the R branch (higher), with few molecules contributing near nu0. In quantum mechanics the rotation is quantized and a third, sharp Q branch appears at the centre when the dipole change has a component along the rotation axis: classical dynamics cannot produce it, which is one reason for the VCI-plus-rotor band shapes later in the deck.

slides.title: VCI, vibrational configuration interaction: mixing simple vibrations
slides.section: Quantum vibrations and rotations: VCI against experiment and the literature
slides.html:
Quantum vibrations · the idea

VCI, vibrational configuration interaction: mixing simple vibrations

1

Simple states first. Treat each of the 9 normal modes as its own spring; a state is how many quanta each one has, e.g. one quantum of C–O stretch.

2

The real surface couples them. States of similar energy mix, like electron configurations in CI.

3

Matrix and diagonalise: 36,890 simple states; each level is named by its largest part.

Why it matters: 2ν₉ has no intensity of its own, but by mixing with ν₄ it borrows some and appears in the spectrum, at 1229 cm⁻¹ (expt. 1234).

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 24 · levels from this work; a grid like DVR in 9-D would need ~10¹² points
slides.notes: For an undergraduate audience. A grid (DVR) works well for 3 or 4 coordinates but its size grows as points to the power of the number of coordinates: 20 points in 9 coordinates is 5 x 10^11 grid points. VCI instead starts from the harmonic picture students know (each normal mode a separate oscillator with levels n h nu) and builds the true states as combinations of a manageable number of these product states, chosen up to a cutoff energy (here 7000 cm-1 for the low modes, up to 3 quanta in the C-H stretches). The name comes from configuration interaction in electronic structure, where Slater determinants (electron configurations) are mixed the same way. The example on the slide is a Fermi resonance: the C-O stretch nu4 and two quanta of the CH2 torsion 2nu9 lie close in energy and the anharmonic surface couples them, so the true levels are mixtures that repel each other. Experiment sees both (Huang et al. 2015 assigned the 1234 band to 2nu9 for this reason). Numbers: harmonic nu4 1308.7, 2 x nu9 harmonic 1274.4; VCI 1275.1 (69% nu4, 21% 2nu9) and 1228.6 (65% 2nu9, 22% nu4).

slides.title: RPMD: each quantum atom a necklace of beads
slides.section: Independent tests: isotopologues, CD2OO and ring-polymer dynamics
slides.html:
Ring-polymer molecular dynamics · the idea

RPMD: each quantum atom a necklace of beads

The trick (Feynman)

In its statistics each quantum atom is a classical ring of P beads on springs (ωP = P kBT/ħ); plain MD of the rings then gives zero-point energy and the spread of the atoms.

Exact for a harmonic bond

Approximate for anharmonic ones: here it closes 25–78% of the gap to VCI.

The springs’ own vibrations

The lowest ring mode is ≈ 2πkBT/hc = 1310 cm⁻¹ at 300 K for any P: on the C–O band. TRPMD damps it with a thermostat, which broadens bands.

Still classical in time

No quantum mixing (Fermi resonances, overtones), no sharp Q branch: those need VCI.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 30 · Craig & Manolopoulos, JCP 121, 3368 (2004); TRPMD: Rossi, Ceriotti & Manolopoulos, JCP 140, 234116 (2014)
slides.notes: For an undergraduate audience. Feynman's path integral says the quantum Boltzmann distribution of a particle is the same as the classical distribution of a closed chain (ring polymer) of P copies, the beads, each feeling 1/P of the potential and joined to its neighbours by harmonic springs of frequency omega_P = P kB T / hbar; the result becomes exact as P grows (the planning stage rpmd_plan shows 97% of the zero-point energy captured at P = 32 for the C-H stretches, 99.8% at P = 128). The ring's size shows the quantum spread of the atom: about 0.16 A for H and a few hundredths of an A for C and O at 300 K. RPMD (Craig and Manolopoulos 2004) goes one step further and runs Newtonian dynamics of the rings, using the bead-averaged dipole to compute the spectrum. Why harmonic springs matter twice. First, for a harmonic potential the ring's centre moves exactly like the quantum oscillator (the Kubo-transformed correlation function is exact), so RPMD is exact in the harmonic limit and errors come only from anharmonicity. Second, the springs between beads are themselves vibrations, with frequencies omega_k = 2 omega_P sin(k pi / P); the lowest tends to 2 pi kB T / hbar, about 1310 cm-1 at 300 K, whatever P is (1308, 2603, 3874 cm-1 for P = 32, drawn on the right). These unphysical vibrations can resonate with real ones, here the C-O stretch, and put spurious peaks or splittings in the spectrum. Thermostatted RPMD (TRPMD, Rossi, Ceriotti and Manolopoulos 2014) attaches a friction to the ring's internal modes only (gamma_k = 2 lambda omega_k, lambda 0.5 here), which removes the resonances but broadens the bands; our friction scan from 0 to 1 did not move the band centres. What remains classical: the motion of the ring's centre, so quantum interference between states (Fermi resonances such as nu4 / 2nu9, overtone and combination bands) and quantized rotation (the Q branch) are missing. That is why TRPMD sits 5-6 cm-1 above VCI on the same surface, and why VCI is the reference wherever it can be done. For MVK-oxide, where VCI cannot cover all 30 modes, TRPMD calibrated this way is the practical quantum method.

slides.notes: Thermostatted ring-polymer molecular dynamics (TRPMD): each atom is a ring of P beads joined by springs; the internal modes of the ring are thermostatted (friction 2 lambda omega_k, lambda 0.5) and the spectrum is the Fourier transform of the Kubo-transformed, bead-averaged dipole autocorrelation. Same surface and dipole as the VCI, so differences are the dynamics alone. Classical reference: 160 trajectories from the ir stage; band centres are intensity-weighted over 870-950, 1250-1340 and 1400-1500 cm-1 with bootstrap error bars (TRPMD errors 0.2-0.6 cm-1). VCI centres are the centres of the VCI contour over the same windows. A friction scan (lambda 0 to 1) changed nothing. TRPMD is known to leave part of the anharmonic shift and to broaden bands through the thermostat (Rossi et al. 2014; Benson and Althorpe 2021 for quasi-centroid MD); here it is quantified on a molecule where the exact answer is available. Cost scales with the number of atoms times P, not exponentially with modes as VCI does: the reason it is the route to MVK-oxide. slides.title: A complementary diabatic neural network carries all the states
slides.section: Beyond the well: the complementary diabatic network for multistate and hot-molecule dynamics
slides.html:
Beyond the well · the multistate surface

A complementary diabatic neural network carries all the states

One small matrix H(R) of chemically labelled states: the ion pair CH₂O⁺ + O⁻ (the well), CH₂O(T₁) + O(³P), CH₂O + O(¹D)

Its eigenvalues are the computed states. The network learns smooth diabats and couplings; crossings and charge transfer follow

What the well surface cannot do: dissociation, the UV states, couplings for surface hopping

The 9-D CCSD(T) surface joins it as a Δ on the diagonal: spectroscopic accuracy in the well, multistate physics beyond

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 34 · learned diabats (dashed) behind CASSCF states along r(O–O); see the “Bridging the Middle Zone” deck
slides.notes: This is the larger model the CH2OO well surface plugs into, and the one we build on for multistate dynamics. Instead of fitting each adiabatic state separately (they have kinks and avoided crossings that a network fits badly), the network predicts a small symmetric matrix H(R) whose diagonal elements are diabatic states with fixed chemical character and whose off-diagonal elements are couplings; diagonalising it gives the adiabatic energies that the electronic-structure calculation produces, and the eigenvectors give the character of each state and the nonadiabatic couplings needed for surface hopping. For CH2OO the diabats are physically framed: the ion pair CH2O+ + O- (the zwitterionic character that makes the Criegee intermediate a bound molecule), CH2O(T1) + O(3P), and the three components of CH2O + O(1D). They cross near r(O-O) 2-2.5 A, which is where the B/C avoided crossing and the UV structure come from (Kuwata 2024) and where hot or photoexcited molecules break the O-O bond. Complementary to the 9-D CCSD(T) surface: the network is trained on multireference (CASSCF/NEVPT2) data and covers every state everywhere at modest accuracy; the CCSD(T) surface is spectroscopically accurate but only for the ground state in the well. The next three slides show how they are joined: Delta = CCSD(T) minus the network's ground state, added to every diagonal element (which leaves gaps and couplings unchanged) and switched off where the states crowd together. The same construction is what we would build for MVK-oxide, whose conformers and resonance-stabilised C=C-C=O-O framework add more diabats. Background on the idea: the "Bridging the Middle Zone" deck.

Toward one surface · the Δ idea

Correct the cheap global surface only where CCSD(T) can be trusted

The network keeps every state and coupling from NEVPT2. CCSD(T) fixes the ground-state well.

Δ is added to every diagonal element, so the gaps, eigenvectors and hopping are unchanged.

A switch w turns Δ off where the states crowd together.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 35 · data: 24_spec and 29_aug, r(C–O) 1.27 Å
slides.notes: Written for an undergraduate audience. Panel 1: NEVPT2 is multireference, so it describes all four states out to CH2O + O(1D), but at cc-pVDZ and with SA4 noise. CCSD(T) is single-reference: accurate in the well (T1 0.03-0.07) and not valid where the states crowd together. Panel 2: Delta = CCSD(T) minus the network's NEVPT2 ground state at the same geometries. Panel 3: a smooth model of Delta (polynomial or GP), multiplied by a switch w that is 1 in the well and 0 past 1.75 A. Panel 5 is why this is safe for dynamics with surface hopping: adding the same number to every diagonal element of the diabatic matrix shifts all adiabatic energies equally and leaves the mixing (eigenvectors) and therefore the nonadiabatic couplings alone. The switch range and the cubic Delta are illustrative; the next slide shows what the switch costs in force.

Toward one surface · what the switch costs

A ramp, not a barrier, and most of it need not be switched

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 36 · 29_aug method check: CCSD(T) and NEVPT2, both aug-cc-pVDZ
slides.notes: The Delta figure plots Delta in meV over a short O-O range, which makes the switch look like a cliff. On the surface's own scale (panel A) it removes about 0.13-0.15 eV (3 kcal/mol) over 0.2 A, while the bond climbs about 2 eV. What trajectories feel is force (panel B): up to about 1.2 eV/A added where the bond force is about 3.3 eV/A, roughly a third, which is enough to change how fast a hot O-O bond stretches. The fix (panel C): most of Delta here is not CCSD(T) versus NEVPT2 at all. The method cut has state-specific NEVPT2 and CCSD(T) in the same aug-cc-pVDZ basis, and their difference is under 5 meV in the well (it grows to about 30 meV at 1.52 A, partly the state-specific upturn). The rest, about 100 meV, is basis and orbital (cc-pVDZ SA4 to aug-cc-pVDZ), and both sides of that are multireference, so it is valid at any O-O and needs no switch. Plan: learn Delta_MR from a NEVPT2 aug-cc-pVDZ cut out to dissociation (about 20 points, still to be measured; the dotted line is a placeholder), apply it everywhere, and switch only Delta_CC. A wider switch alone does not help much here because Delta is still changing at the edge of the data.

slides.title: A Gaussian process says where it is unsure; a polynomial does not
slides.section: Beyond the well: the complementary diabatic network for multistate and hot-molecule dynamics
slides.html:
Toward one surface · fitting Δ

A Gaussian process says where it is unsure; a polynomial does not

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 37 · GP: diabml.gpdelta, Matérn 5/2, fitted length scale 0.18 Å
slides.notes: Same 11 Delta points as the Delta figure. A polynomial is one global formula: it fits the points well but carries its trend past the data, here diving to -400 meV by 1.7 A, and gives no warning. A GP builds the curve from the data with a kernel that sets the smoothness; with a zero prior mean it relaxes back to no correction over about one length scale (0.18 A here) and its error band widens as it does. That error band comes from the same fit: it drives the choice of the next shell batches (largest sigma) and, by drawing posterior samples, gives error bars on the fundamentals. Limits: sigma is interpolation error only, not the error of CCSD(T); it must be checked on held-out batches (shell_check does). The GP's own relaxation to zero is a soft switch, but its length scale is learned from the well, so the explicit switch w stays. Use: polynomial for the dense, smooth well data in vib_levels; GP for Delta on the network across the sparse shell.

slides.notes: Done since the 4 November version: the 9-D CCSD(T) surface with a 9-D aug-cc-pVTZ correction and CCSD(T) dipole; VCI with Coriolis coupling; rotational band shapes; isotopologue microwave constants and CD2OO; classical and TRPMD spectra on the same surface; CCSD(T) checks at bead geometries and the extension to 1.5 eV. For MVKO the first decision is the cheap base surface (wB97X-D or B3LYP, aug basis) and how many CCSD(T) Delta points per conformer; the CH2OO numbers (250 points for a 9-D Delta to 4 meV) give a starting estimate. The 13 kJ/mol emission is already computed by VCI for CH2OO (hot bands, T_vib 691 K) and is ready to compare with the emission experiment. For hot molecules, the kinetic benchmark is Stone et al., PCCP 20, 24940 (2018): decomposition rates of CH2OO and CD2OO over 450-650 K and the product branching, a test of the surface at the dioxirane barrier (about 80 kJ/mol, 0.8 eV) and of the isotope effect.

Earlier summary: four findings from the 3-D and 4-D work

1 · The surface set the band positions

The NN ensemble could not fix the curvature at the minimum, and the SA4 reference data scattered 5–50 meV between points.
